A.3. A review of exponential mixed Hodge structures

Let 𝔸θ1\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta} be the affine line with coordinate θ\theta. In [36, §4], Kontsevich and Soibelman define the category 𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\EMHS of exponential mixed Hodge structures as the full subcategory of 𝖬𝖧𝖬⁡(𝔸θ1)\MHM(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}) consisting of those objects NHN^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}} whose underlying perverse sheaf has vanishing global cohomology. The assignment

NH⟼Πθ(NH)=NH⋆j!H𝒪𝔾mH,N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}\mathchoice{\longmapsto}{\mapsto}{\mapsto}{\mapsto}\Pi_{\theta}(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}})=N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}\star{}_{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}j_{!}\mathscr{O}_{\mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}},

where ⋆\star stands for additive ∗\ast-convolution defined as

(A.5) N1H⋆N2H=s∗H​(N1H⊠N2H)N_{1}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}\star N_{2}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}={}_{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}s_{*}(N_{1}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}\boxtimes N_{2}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}})

and j:𝔾m↪𝔸1j\colon\mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{A}^{\!1} for the inclusion, yields an exact functor Πθ:𝖬𝖧𝖬⁡(𝔸θ1)→𝖬𝖧𝖬⁡(𝔸θ1)\Pi_{\theta}\colon\MHM(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta})\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\MHM(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}), which is a projector onto 𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\EMHS that is left adjoint to its inclusion as a subcategory. In particular, there is a natural morphism NH→Πθ​(NH)N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\Pi_{\theta}(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) in 𝖬𝖧𝖬⁡(𝔸θ1)\MHM(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}). Its kernel and cokernel are constant mixed Hodge modules on 𝔸θ1\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}. More precisely, the 𝒟𝔸θ1\mathscr{D}_{\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}}-module underlying the kernel is the maximal constant submodule of NN. We will also write Π\Pi for Πθ\Pi_{\theta} when the coordinate is clear.

Each object of 𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\EMHS is endowed with a weight filtration, defined from that in 𝖬𝖧𝖬⁡(𝔸θ1)\MHM(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}) by the formula WnEMHS​Π​(NH)=Π⁡(Wn​NH)W^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{EMHS}}_{n}\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}})=\Pi(W_{n}N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) for any mixed Hodge module NHN^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}} on 𝔸θ1\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}.

Remark A.6.

This weight filtration has the following properties:

  • ∙\scriptscriptstyle\bullet

    if N=Π⁡(N)N=\Pi(N) (and hence NH=Π⁡(NH)N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}=\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}})) there is a functorial morphism

    Wn​NH⟶WnEMHS​NH;W_{n}N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}W^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{EMHS}}_{n}N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}};
  • ∙\scriptscriptstyle\bullet

    if NHN^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}} is mixed of weights ⩽n\leqslant n (resp. ⩾n\geqslant n) in 𝖬𝖧𝖬⁡(𝔸θ1)\MHM(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}), then Π⁡(NH)\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) is mixed of weights ⩽n\leqslant n (resp. ⩾n\geqslant n) in 𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\EMHS; therefore, if NHN^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}} is pure of weight nn, then Π⁡(NH)\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) (which in general is mixed of weights ⩾n\geqslant n as an object of 𝖬𝖧𝖬⁡(𝔸θ1)\MHM(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta})) is a pure object of 𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\EMHS of weight nn.

  • ∙\scriptscriptstyle\bullet

    For the sake of simplicity, when there is no risk of confusion, we write W∙​Π​(NH)W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) instead of W∙EMHS​Π​(NH)W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{EMHS}}\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) for the weight filtration of an exponential mixed Hodge structure Π⁡(NH)\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}).

The category 𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\EMHS is endowed with a tensor structure induced by the additive convolution ⋆\star on 𝖬𝖧𝖬⁡(𝔸1)\MHM(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}) such that the equality

Π⁡(N1H)⋆Π⁡(N2H)=Π⁡(N1H⋆N2H)\Pi(N_{1}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}})\star\Pi(N_{2}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}})=\Pi(N_{1}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}\star N_{2}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}})

holds. Moreover, the weight filtration is strictly compatible with the tensor product (see [36, Prop. 4.3]). Note that N1H⋆N2HN_{1}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}\star N_{2}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}} could be a complex, but its cohomologies in non-zero degrees are constant (this is checked on the underlying 𝒟\mathscr{D}-modules), and hence are annihilated by Π\Pi; on the other hand, the cohomology of Π⁡(N1H)⋆Π⁡(N2H)\Pi(N_{1}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}})\star\Pi(N_{2}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) is concentrated in degree zero.

Recall that the functor

(A.7) 𝖬𝗈𝖽holreg​(𝒟𝔸θ1)⟶𝖵𝖾𝖼𝗍𝐂,N⟼HdR1​(𝔸θ1,N⊗Eθ)\mathsf{Mod}_{{\mathrm{hol}}\mathrm{reg}}(\mathscr{D}_{\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}})\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\mathsf{Vect}_{\mathbf{C}},\quad N\mathchoice{\longmapsto}{\mapsto}{\mapsto}{\mapsto}\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N\otimes E^{\theta})

is exact and that HdRj​(𝔸θ1,N⊗Eθ)\mathrm{H}^{j}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N\otimes E^{\theta}) vanishes for j≠1j\neq 1. Moreover, the morphism N→Π⁡(N)N\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\Pi(N) induces an isomorphism

HdR1​(𝔸θ1,N⊗Eθ)⟶HdR1​(𝔸θ1,Π⁡(N)⊗Eθ).\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N\otimes E^{\theta})\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},\Pi(N)\otimes E^{\theta}).

Let NHN^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}} be a mixed Hodge module on 𝔸θ1\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}, and let Π⁡(NH)\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) be the associated object in 𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\EMHS. Let a𝔸θ1a_{\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}} denote the structure morphism of 𝔸θ1\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}. The de Rham fiber functor on 𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\EMHS is given by

(A.8) Π⁡(NH)⟼HdR1​(𝔸θ1,Π⁡(N)⊗Eθ)=HdR1​(𝔸θ1,N⊗Eθ)=H0​a𝔸θ1,+​(N⊗Eθ).\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}})\mathchoice{\longmapsto}{\mapsto}{\mapsto}{\mapsto}\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},\Pi(N)\otimes E^{\theta})=\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N\otimes E^{\theta})=\mathrm{H}^{0}a_{\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},+}(N\otimes E^{\theta}).

An object of 𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\EMHS is zero if and only if its de Rham fiber is zero. It follows from the exactness of (A.7) that the natural morphism

(A.9) HdR1​(𝔸θ1,W∙​N⊗Eθ)⟶HdR1​(𝔸θ1,N⊗Eθ)\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}N\otimes E^{\theta})\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N\otimes E^{\theta})

is injective. The filtration W∙​HdR1​(𝔸θ1,N⊗Eθ)W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N\otimes E^{\theta}) is defined as its image. Then any morphism N1H→N2HN_{1}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}N_{2}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}} induces a strictly filtered morphism

(HdR1​(𝔸θ1,N1⊗Eθ),W∙)⟶(HdR1​(𝔸θ1,N2⊗Eθ),W∙).(\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N_{1}\otimes E^{\theta}),W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet})\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}(\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N_{2}\otimes E^{\theta}),W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}).

On the other hand, letting j∞:𝔸θ1⸦→ℙθ1j_{\infty}\colon\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}\mathrel{\lhook\joinrel\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}}\mathbb{P}^{1}_{\theta} denote the inclusion, the (decreasing) irregular Hodge filtration on j∞+​(N⊗Eθ)j_{\infty+}(N\otimes E^{\theta}) is defined in [50, §6.b] out of the Hodge filtration F∙​NF^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}N of NHN^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}. It is indexed by 𝐐\mathbf{Q} and denoted by FDel∙F_{\mathrm{Del}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet} in loc. cit., whereas here we denote it by Firr∙F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}, to emphasize the compatibility with other possible definitions [15, 52].

Proposition A.10.

The natural morphism

HdR1​(ℙθ1,Firr∙​j∞+​(N⊗Eθ))⟶HdR1​(ℙθ1,j∞+​(N⊗Eθ))=HdR1​(𝔸θ1,N⊗Eθ)\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{P}^{1}_{\theta},F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}j_{\infty+}(N\otimes E^{\theta}))\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{P}^{1}_{\theta},j_{\infty+}(N\otimes E^{\theta}))=\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N\otimes E^{\theta})

is injective and, defining Firr∙​HdR1​(𝔸θ1,N⊗Eθ)F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N\otimes E^{\theta}) as its image, the functor from 𝖬𝖧𝖬⁡(𝔸θ1)\MHM(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}) to bifiltered vector spaces

(A.11) NH⟼(HdR1​(𝔸θ1,N⊗Eθ),Firr∙,W∙)N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}\mathchoice{\longmapsto}{\mapsto}{\mapsto}{\mapsto}\bigl(\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N\otimes E^{\theta}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet})

factors through Π\Pi. Any morphism in 𝖬𝖧𝖬⁡(𝔸θ1)\MHM(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}) (or in 𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\EMHS) gives rise by means of (A.11) to a strictly bifiltered morphism.

Proof.

Injectivity is proved in [50, Th. 6.1] for polarized Hodge modules. The case of mixed Hodge modules is deduced from it in [15, Th. 3.3.1] (in a more general setting). Since the kernel and the cokernel of NH→Π⁡(NH)N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) are constant mixed Hodge modules and HdRj​(𝔸θ1,N⊗Eθ)\mathrm{H}^{j}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N\otimes E^{\theta}) vanishes in all degrees jj for constant NN, it is clear that (A.11) factors through Π\Pi. The last statement is obtained by successively applying Theorems 0.2(2), 0.3(4), and 0.3(2) of [51]. ∎

A.4. Mixed Hodge structures as exponential mixed Hodge structures

Let 𝖬𝖧𝖲\MHS be the category of mixed Hodge structures, endowed with its natural tensor product. We consider the open immersion j0:𝔾m⸦→𝔸θ1j_{0}\colon\mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}}\mathrel{\lhook\joinrel\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}}\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta} and the closed immersion i0:{0}⸦→𝔸θ1i_{0}\colon\{0\}\mathrel{\lhook\joinrel\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}}\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}. Letting i0!H{}_{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}i_{0!} denote the pushforward functor 𝖬𝖧𝖲→𝖬𝖧𝖬⁡(𝔸θ1)\MHS\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\MHM(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}), there is an isomorphism ϕθ,1∘i0!H≃Id𝖬𝖧𝖲\phi_{\theta,1}\circ{}_{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}i_{0!}\simeq\id_{\MHS}. Let us now consider the composed functor Π∘i0!H:𝖬𝖧𝖲→𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\Pi\circ{}_{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}i_{0!}:\MHS\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\EMHS. Then there is an isomorphism ϕθ,1∘(Π∘i0!H)≃Id𝖬𝖧𝖲\phi_{\theta,1}\circ(\Pi\circ{}_{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}i_{0!})\simeq\id_{\MHS}, since ϕθ,1∘Π≃ϕθ,1\phi_{\theta,1}\circ\Pi\simeq\phi_{\theta,1} (because ϕθ,1\phi_{\theta,1} of a constant object in 𝖬𝖧𝖬⁡(𝔸θ1)\MHM(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}) is zero). From standard properties of mixed Hodge modules one checks the following lemma.

Lemma A.12.

The functor Π∘i0!H:𝖬𝖧𝖲→𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\Pi\circ{}_{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}i_{0!}\colon\MHS\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\EMHS is compatible with tensor products and makes 𝖬𝖧𝖲\MHS into a full tensor subcategory of 𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\EMHS. Moreover, if VHV^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}} is a mixed Hodge structure with weight filtration W∙​VHW_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}V^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}} and associated exponential mixed Hodge structure Πθ​(i0!H​VH)\Pi_{\theta}({}_{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}i_{0!}V^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}), then the equality W∙​Πθ​(i0!H​VH)=Πθ​(i0!H​W∙​VH)W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}\Pi_{\theta}({}_{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}i_{0!}V^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}})=\Pi_{\theta}({}_{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}i_{0!}W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}V^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) holds (see Remark A.6 for the notation).

Proposition A.13.

Let NHN^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}} be an object of 𝖬𝖧𝖬⁡(𝔸θ1)\MHM(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}) such that Π⁡(NH)\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) belongs to 𝖬𝖧𝖲\MHS. Then the bifiltered vector space (HdR1​(𝔸θ1,N⊗Eθ),Firr∙,W∙)\bigl(\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N\otimes E^{\theta}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}) is naturally isomorphic to that associated with the mixed Hodge structure ϕθ,1​NH\phi_{\theta,1}N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}.

Proof.

Let VHV^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}} be a mixed Hodge structure. The vector space (HdR1​(𝔸θ1,i0+​V⊗Eθ),Firr∙,W∙)\bigl(\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},i_{0+}V\otimes E^{\theta}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}) endowed with its two filtrations is easily identified with (V,F∙,W∙)(V,F^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}). Taking the isomorphism

(HdR1​(𝔸θ1,Π⁡(i0+​V)⊗Eθ),Firr∙,W∙)≃(HdR1​(𝔸θ1,i0+​V⊗Eθ),Firr∙,W∙)\bigl(\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},\Pi(i_{0+}V)\otimes E^{\theta}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet})\simeq\bigl(\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},i_{0+}V\otimes E^{\theta}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet})

into account, we deduce an isomorphism

(A.14) (HdR1​(𝔸θ1,Π⁡(i0+​V)⊗Eθ),Firr∙,W∙)≃(V,F∙,W∙).\bigl(\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},\Pi(i_{0+}V)\otimes E^{\theta}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet})\simeq(V,F^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}).

Now, if Π⁡(NH)\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) belongs to 𝖬𝖧𝖲\MHS, then Π⁡(NH)=Π⁡(i0!H​VH)\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}})=\Pi({}_{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}i_{0!}V^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) for some mixed Hodge structure VHV^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}, which satisfies VH≃ϕθ,1​Π​(NH)≃ϕθ,1​NHV^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}\simeq\phi_{\theta,1}\Pi(N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}})\simeq\phi_{\theta,1}N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}. Then (A.14) gives

(ϕθ,1​N,F∙,W∙)\displaystyle(\phi_{\theta,1}N,F^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}) ≃(HdR1​(𝔸θ1,Π⁡(i0+​ϕθ,1​N)⊗Eθ),Firr∙,W∙)\displaystyle\simeq\bigl(\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},\Pi(i_{0+}\phi_{\theta,1}N)\otimes E^{\theta}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet})
≃(HdR1​(𝔸θ1,Π⁡(N)⊗Eθ),Firr∙,W∙)\displaystyle\simeq\bigl(\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},\Pi(N)\otimes E^{\theta}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet})
≃(HdR1​(𝔸θ1,N⊗Eθ),Firr∙,W∙),\displaystyle\simeq\bigl(\mathrm{H}^{1}_{{\mathrm{dR}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta},N\otimes E^{\theta}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}),

as we wanted to show. ∎

on 𝔸θ1\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}, and we denote by Nr∗,Nr!,NrmidN^{r}_{*},N^{r}_{!},N^{r}_{\mathrm{mid}} the respective underlying 𝒟𝔸θ1\mathscr{D}_{\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta}}-modules. Upon application of the projector Πθ\Pi_{\theta}, they define objects of 𝖤𝖬𝖧𝖲\EMHS:

Let aUa_{U} denote the structure morphism of UU. For ff the zero function, the above are the mixed Hodge structures

This follows from [52, Th. 1.3(4)] applied to a compactification of the morphism ff and by taking the pushforward by the structure morphism. The natural morphism (HdR,cr​(U,NU⊗Ef),Firr∙)→(HdRr​(U,NU⊗Ef),Firr∙)(\mathrm{H}^{r}_{{\mathrm{dR}},{\mathrm{c}}}(U,N_{U}\otimes E^{f}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet})\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}(\mathrm{H}^{r}_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,N_{U}\otimes E^{f}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}) is strict and its image HdR,midr​(U,NU⊗Ef)\mathrm{H}^{r}_{{\mathrm{dR}},{\mathrm{mid}}}(U,N_{U}\otimes E^{f}) is endowed with the quotient (equivalently sub) filtration Firr∙F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}.

Definition A.20 ([36, §5]).

Associated with a function f:U→𝔸θ1f\colon U\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\theta} and an integer rr as above are the exponential mixed Hodge structures

Hr(U,f)=Πθ((p𝐐UH)∗r),Hcr(U,f)=Πθ((p𝐐UH)!r),Hmidr(U,f)=Πθ((p𝐐UH)midr),\mathrm{H}^{r}(U,f)=\Pi_{\theta}((\raisebox{6.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}$}{\mathbf{Q}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}_{U})^{r}_{*}),\quad\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{c}}^{r}(U,f)=\Pi_{\theta}((\raisebox{6.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}$}{\mathbf{Q}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}_{U})^{r}_{!}),\quad\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{mid}}^{r}(U,f)=\Pi_{\theta}((\raisebox{6.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}$}{\mathbf{Q}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}_{U})^{r}_{\mathrm{mid}}),

with corresponding bifiltered de Rham fibers

(HdRr​(U,Ef),Firr∙,W∙),(HdR,cr​(U,Ef),Firr∙,W∙),(HdR,midr​(U,Ef),Firr∙,W∙).(\mathrm{H}^{r}_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,E^{f}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}),\quad(\mathrm{H}^{r}_{{\mathrm{dR}},{\mathrm{c}}}(U,E^{f}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}),\quad(\mathrm{H}^{r}_{{\mathrm{dR}},{\mathrm{mid}}}(U,E^{f}),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}).
Proposition A.21.

The exponential mixed Hodge structure Hcd​(U,f)\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{c}}^{d}(U,f) is mixed of weights ⩽d\leqslant d, Hd​(U,f)\mathrm{H}^{d}(U,f) is mixed of weights ⩾d\geqslant d, and Hmidd​(U,f)\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{mid}}^{d}(U,f) is pure of weight dd. Moreover, the following properties are equivalent:

    the natural morphism grdW​Hcd​(U,f)→grdW​Hd​(U,f)\gr_{d}^{W}\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{c}}^{d}(U,f)\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\gr_{d}^{W}\mathrm{H}^{d}(U,f) is an isomorphism,

    the equality Hmidd​(U,f)=Wd​Hd​(U,f)\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{mid}}^{d}(U,f)=W_{d}\mathrm{H}^{d}(U,f) holds.

The de Rham fibers of Hj+1​(𝔸t1×𝔸τ1,NH,t​τ)\mathrm{H}^{j+1}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{t}\times\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\tau},N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}},t\tau) and Hcj+1​(𝔸t1×𝔸τ1,NH,t​τ)\mathrm{H}^{j+1}_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{t}\times\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\tau},N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}},t\tau) are, respectively, HdRj​(𝔸t1,FT⁡M)\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{dR}}^{j}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{t},\FT M) for j=0,1j=0,1 and HdR,cj​(𝔸t1,FT⁡M)\mathrm{H}_{{\mathrm{dR}},{\mathrm{c}}}^{j}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{t},\FT M) for j=1,2j=1,2, and zero otherwise.

Notation A.31.

We denote by Hj​(𝔸t1,FT⁡MH)\mathrm{H}^{j}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{t},\FT M^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) and Hcj​(𝔸t1,FT⁡MH)\mathrm{H}^{j}_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{t},\FT M^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}}) the mixed Hodge structure Hj+1​(𝔸t1×𝔸τ1,NH,t​τ)\mathrm{H}^{j+1}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{t}\times\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\tau},N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}},t\tau) and Hcj+1​(𝔸t1×𝔸τ1,NH,t​τ)\mathrm{H}^{j+1}_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{t}\times\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{\tau},N^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{H}},t\tau) respectively. Their associated bifiltered de Rham fibers are (HdRj​(𝔸t1,FT⁡M),Firr∙,W∙)(\mathrm{H}^{j}_{\mathrm{dR}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{t},\FT M),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{${\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}$}},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}) and (HdR,cj​(𝔸t1,FT⁡M),Firr∙,W∙)(\mathrm{H}^{j}_{{\mathrm{dR}},{\mathrm{c}}}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{t},\FT M),F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{${\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}$}},W_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}).

A priori, there might be a source of ambiguity in the notation for the irregular Hodge filtration, since FT⁡M\FT M also underlies an irregular mixed Hodge module on ℙt1\mathbb{P}^{1}_{t} in the sense of [51], by means of which HdRj​(𝔸t1,FT⁡M)\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{dR}}^{j}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}_{t},\FT M) acquires an irregular Hodge filtration. We shall not use this property.
